newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says cuts April govt-backed,municipal coupon.
newsitem.headline: Japan says cuts April govt-backed,municipal coupon.

text.p: The coupon rate for April issues of Japanese government-guaranteed and municipal bonds was set at a record low of 2.4 percent, down from 2.6 percent for the March issues, the finance and home ministries said on Thursday.
The price of the April government-guaranteed bonds was set at 99.50 and that of the April municipal bonds at 99.40, the ministries said.

Traders said demand for these long-term bonds was expected to be subdued because the coupon rate was lower than the 2.5 percent for the April 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) issue whose terms were set through a price-competitive auction the Ministry of Finance (MOF) held on March 25.
The 10-year JGB auction produced an average price of 99.95 and a lowest price of 99.90.
A MOF official said the rate cut for government-backed bonds reflected the sharp fall in market yields of JGBs in recent sessions.
The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGB hit a record low of 2.140 percent on Wednesday.
The MOF said it was planning only one government-guaranteed bond issue for April in a volume of 350 billion yen.
The total amount of municipal bonds to be issued by six regional governments in April is 168 billion yen, the Ministry of Home Affairs said.
